# Research-Gap Report: Reinforcement Learning Robotics

---

## Domain Landscape

The RL-robotics literature organizes into three mature, high-volume clusters—**locomotion** (39 papers, mean year 2020.3), **navigation** (31, 2020.2), and **deep RL applications** (25, 2019.4)—alongside active mid-size clusters in human–robot interaction (22, 2018.6), imitation/demonstration learning (21, 2019.6), and manipulation/grasping (20, 2019.2). Emerging threads include safety-constrained control (14, 2020.9), precision assembly (13, 2020.5), and soft robotics (9, 2020.8). The overall center of gravity sits in 2019–2020, indicating a field that has recently consolidated core deep-RL techniques for individual sub-problems but has not yet systematically bridged them.

---

## Validated Gaps

### Gap 1 — Whole-Body Navigation: Integrating Bipedal Locomotion with Mobile-Robot Navigation
**Confidence: 1.0 (CONFIRMED)**

**Why it is a gap:** The locomotion cluster (size 39) and the navigation cluster (size 31) share 241 bridge papers, yet a prominence score of only 0.18 and **zero recent papers** returned for the direct queries `"bipedal walking" + "robot navigation"` and `"humanoid locomotion" + "mobile robot environments"` confirm that these two bodies of work have not been jointly addressed in current research. Work on legged locomotion optimizes gait and stability in isolation, while navigation research assumes a kinematically simple mobile base; the compound problem of a bipedal or humanoid robot planning and executing navigation in unstructured environments remains open.

**Research Agenda:**
1. **Benchmark development** — Create standardized simulation and real-world benchmarks that couple terrain-adaptive locomotion with goal-directed navigation tasks (e.g., traverse rough terrain to reach a waypoint), enabling apples-to-apples comparison of joint vs. hierarchical policies.
2. **Hierarchical policy architecture** — Design a two-level RL framework in which a high-level navigation planner generates locomotion-aware waypoints and a low-level locomotion controller executes them, with gradient or reward signal flowing between levels.
3. **Sim-to-real transfer evaluation** — Systematically test the combined policy on physical bipedal/humanoid platforms, quantifying the additional domain-gap costs introduced by coupling the two sub-problems.

---

### Gap 2 — Loco-Manipulation: Coupling Bipedal Walking with Task-Directed Object Interaction
**Confidence: 0.96 (CONFIRMED)**

**Why it is a gap:** The locomotion cluster (size 39) and the human/tasks cluster (size 22) share 243 bridge papers, yet a prominence score of 0.14 and only **1 recent paper** found for the queries `"bipedal walking" + "object manipulation"` and `"humanoid locomotion" + "task reward"` indicate that joint locomotion–task-execution policies are nearly absent from current literature. Existing reward shaping and task-completion research assumes a stationary or wheeled base, while locomotion work ignores task objectives entirely.

**Research Agenda:**
1. **Composite reward design** — Investigate reward formulations that simultaneously encode locomotion stability, energy efficiency, and task-completion criteria (e.g., pick-and-place while walking), studying trade-offs and shaping strategies.
2. **Unified policy learning** — Train end-to-end RL agents on loco-manipulation tasks in simulation, comparing monolithic policies against modular architectures that share a latent representation of body state and task context.
3. **Human-study evaluation** — Assess learned behaviors against human expectations of naturalness and safety in human-proximate environments, closing the loop with the human–robot interaction literature.

---

### Gap 3 — Dexterous Grasping on Legged Platforms *(Weak Signal — Early Exploration Warranted)*
**Confidence: 0.68 (WEAK)**

**Why it is a gap (with caveats):** The locomotion cluster (size 39) and the manipulation/grasping cluster (size 20) share 244 bridge papers, but a prominence score of 0.14 and **8 recent papers** on `"bipedal walking" + "robotic manipulation"` and `"humanoid robot" + "dexterous grasping"` place this at the boundary between emerging research and a true gap. Activity exists but remains sparse relative to the individual cluster sizes, suggesting the integration of dexterous hand control with whole-body locomotion dynamics is only beginning to be tackled.

**Research Agenda:**
1. **Systematic literature audit** — Catalog the 8 identified papers to characterize which sub-problems (arm–leg coordination, reactive grasping under motion disturbance, etc.) remain unaddressed and where duplication exists.
2. **Disturbance-aware manipulation policies** — Develop RL controllers that explicitly model locomotion-induced base perturbations as disturbances to the grasping task, training policies robust to dynamic base motion.
3. **Longitudinal monitoring** — Re-evaluate publication volume in 6–12 months; if paper count remains below ~20, escalate to a confirmed gap; if it accelerates rapidly, reframe as a fast-moving frontier requiring survey rather than gap-filling work.

---

## Rejected Candidates

Five candidate gaps were rejected due to abundant recent literature: locomotion × deep RL (34 papers), navigation × deep RL (113), locomotion × demonstrations (62), deep RL × human/tasks (189,542), and deep RL × manipulation (173) — all indicating active or saturated research fronts rather than genuine gaps.
